error_modes.label: IDENTIFICATION OF THE SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS OF THE TRAINING EXERCISE

texts.0: SP, due to mission planning that did not address the special items published for the training unit, did not identify which requirements of the Training Exercises analysis applied to this sortie. SP briefed a standard instrument profile and was unable to state the directed special requirements when questioned before start. The IP intervened, re-briefed the applicable items in full and had the mission plan rebuilt before taxi.
texts.1: SP, due to a currency shortfall that was not addressed in the mission planning phase, did not extract all special requirements of the exercise from the Training Exercises analysis. SP listed part of the directed items and completed the list only after being told point by point by the IP what remained outstanding. The brief was eventually correct, but the content came from IP direction rather than from SP's own preparation.
texts.2: SP, due to a first pass through the syllabus exercise sheet that stopped at the maneuver list, did not initially identify one of the special requirements attached to the training unit. SP re-opened the exercise analysis while still in the briefing room, found the missing item and included it in the profile and in the brief. The identification was completed on SP's own initiative, without IP prompting and without delay to the planned start.
texts.3: SP identified the special requirements of the training exercise correctly and completely, as determined by the Training Exercises analysis and the Performance Standards. SP stated each directed item, the level required for this training unit and the point of the profile at which it would be flown. No IP input was required at any stage of the preparation.
texts.4: SP identified every special requirement of the training exercise without reference to notes and related each one to the required MIF level for the unit. SP also stated where each item would be inserted in the profile and what would be given up if airspace or weather forced a change. The preparation was complete and accurate before the IP had raised the subject.
texts.marginal: SP identified the special requirements of the training exercise and the brief met the standard. However, SP recovered two of the directed items only after a visible search through the syllabus material, and the required level for the training unit was stated hesitantly. SP is expected to consolidate the exercise analysis into a single prepared list so that the special requirements are stated from knowledge rather than reconstructed in the briefing room.

texts_at.0: SP identified the special requirements of the training exercise with the IP supplying the outstanding items point by point on the first pass and calling the reference for SP to check on the second. Extracting the complete list of special requirements from the Training Exercises analysis without a cue has not yet been learned. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to extract the complete list independently as the preparation becomes familiar.
texts_at.1: SP identified the special requirements of the training exercise with part of the directed items listed before the remainder was supplied point by point by the IP, due to a currency shortfall that was not addressed in the mission planning phase. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to address any currency shortfall in the mission planning phase itself, not while stating the requirements.
texts_at.2: SP identified the special requirements of the training exercise with one item found only after re-opening the exercise analysis in the briefing room, due to a first pass through the syllabus exercise sheet that stopped at the maneuver list. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to read the full exercise analysis on the first pass, not only the maneuver list.
texts_at.3: SP identified the special requirements of the training exercise correctly and completely, as determined by the Training Exercises analysis and the Performance Standards, with the required level for the training unit stated a beat more hesitantly than the rest of the brief. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to state the required level with the same confidence as the rest of the identification.

texts_above.1: SP identified the special requirements of the training exercise with part of the directed items listed before the remainder was supplied point by point. The remainder came as verbal calls from the IP naming each outstanding item. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP re-opened the exercise analysis while still in the briefing room, found the missing item and included it in the profile and in the brief, on its own initiative and without delay to the planned start. Reading the full exercise analysis on the first pass, not only the maneuver list, would remove the need for that second look. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to good exercise-analysis discipline.
texts_above.3: SP identified the special requirements of the training exercise correctly and completely, as determined by the Training Exercises analysis and the Performance Standards, stating each directed item, the level required for this training unit and the point of the profile at which it would be flown. The only refinement available is to state the required level with the same confidence as the rest of the identification. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to very good exercise-analysis discipline.
texts_above.4: SP identified every special requirement of the training exercise without reference to notes and related each one to the required MIF level for the unit, stating where each item would be inserted in the profile and what would be given up if airspace or weather forced a change. There is little left to refine; the preparation is already complete before the IP raises the subject. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to excellent exercise-analysis discipline.

error_modes.label: ACCOMPLISHMENT OF THE DIRECTED SPECIAL REQUIREMENT ITEMS

texts.0: SP, due to a profile flown from habit rather than from the exercise card, did not accomplish the special requirements directed for this training unit. Two of the directed items were left unflown and the sortie was continued toward recovery with fuel still available for them. The IP intervened, took the aircraft back to the working area and directed the outstanding items to be flown.
texts.1: SP, due to a working sequence that was not checked against the exercise card, did not accomplish one of the directed special requirements at the planned point of the profile. SP flew the item only after repeated verbal reminders from the IP that it remained outstanding, and with the fuel state already at the limit for the working phase. All directed items were finally covered, but only through IP prompting and with the profile compressed.
texts.2: SP, due to a re-sequencing of the profile after the controller withheld the requested block, did not fly one special requirement at the briefed point. SP recognized the omission while still in the working area, requested a further block and completed the item within the planned working time. All directed requirements were accomplished without IP intervention.
texts.3: SP accomplished all the special requirements directed for the training unit, each one flown in full and at the planned point of the profile. SP tracked the exercise card through the sortie and confirmed completion of each item before moving to the next segment. No item was omitted and no IP intervention was required.
texts.4: SP accomplished every directed special requirement of the training unit, complete and in the briefed order, and still had working time and fuel in hand at the end. SP absorbed a change of working area without dropping any item, simply re-ordering the sequence. Nothing had to be repeated and no IP input of any kind was needed.
texts.marginal: SP accomplished all the special requirements directed for the training unit, so the standard was met. However, the last two items were flown in a compressed sequence at the end of the working phase, leaving no margin for a repeat had one been required. SP is expected to distribute the directed items earlier in the profile so that completion does not depend on the remaining fuel.

texts_at.0: SP accomplished the special requirements with the IP tracking the exercise card on the first sortie and calling the outstanding item for SP to fly on the second. Checking the working sequence against the exercise card without a cue has not yet been learned. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to track the exercise card and accomplish the items independently as the habit becomes established.
texts_at.1: SP accomplished the special requirements directed for the training unit, with one item flown only after repeated verbal reminders that it remained outstanding, due to a working sequence that was not checked against the exercise card. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to check the working sequence against the exercise card at each segment, not only near recovery.
texts_at.2: SP accomplished the special requirements directed for the training unit, with one item re-sequenced after the controller withheld the requested block, due to a re-sequencing of the profile that displaced one item from the briefed point. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to hold a backup point in the profile for every item in case the requested block is not available.
texts_at.3: SP accomplished all the special requirements directed for the training unit, each one flown in full and at the planned point of the profile, with completion of the last item confirmed a beat later than the others. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to confirm completion of every item with the same timing as the others.

texts_above.1: SP accomplished the special requirements directed for the training unit, with one item flown only after repeated verbal reminders that it remained outstanding. The reminders came as verbal calls from the IP. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the omission while still in the working area, requested a further block and completed the item within the planned working time, without IP intervention, after one item had initially been displaced from the briefed point by a re-sequencing of the profile. Holding a backup point in the profile for every item would remove the need for that request. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to dependable exercise-card discipline.
texts_above.3: SP accomplished all the special requirements directed for the training unit, each one flown in full and at the planned point of the profile, tracking the exercise card through the sortie and confirming completion of each item before moving to the next segment. The only refinement available is to confirm completion of every item with the same timing as the others. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to notably good exercise-card discipline.
texts_above.4: SP accomplished every directed special requirement of the training unit, complete and in the briefed order, and still had working time and fuel in hand at the end, absorbing a change of working area without dropping any item by simply re-ordering the sequence. There is little left to refine; nothing ever has to be repeated. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to superior exercise-card discipline.

error_modes.label: STANDARD ACHIEVED ON THE SPECIAL REQUIREMENT AGAINST THE MIF LEVEL

texts.0: SP, due to technique that had not been consolidated before the sortie, did not perform the directed special requirement to the level set by the Performance Standards for this training unit. The item was flown with the profile broken twice and the parameters never stabilized, well below the required MIF level. The IP intervened, took control and demonstrated the item before it was attempted again.
texts.1: SP, due to control inputs applied without a settled reference, did not reach the MIF level required for the directed special requirement on the first attempt. The item was completed at the lower limit of acceptability and only after continuous verbal guidance from the IP through each stage. The standard was eventually touched, but the performance depended on the running commentary from the front cockpit.
texts.2: SP, due to an initial entry flown from an unsettled aircraft state, did not achieve the required standard on the first presentation of the directed special requirement. SP recognized the shortfall, reset the parameters and reflew the item to a level between the required and the fully proficient standard. The correction was made on SP's own initiative and no IP intervention was needed.
texts.3: SP performed the directed special requirement to the level required by the Performance Standards for this training unit, accurately and without delay. Entry parameters were established before the item was begun and were held throughout its execution. The required MIF level was met on the first presentation and without IP intervention.
texts.4: SP performed the directed special requirement to a standard above the level set for this training unit, with deviations that were negligible throughout. Entry, execution and recovery were flown as one continuous sequence with no correcting input of any significance. The item required no repetition and no comment from the IP.
texts.marginal: SP performed the directed special requirement to the level required by the Performance Standards, so the standard was met. However, the required level was reached only on the second presentation and the parameters wandered close to the tolerance during the first half of the item. SP is expected to stabilize the entry conditions before beginning the item so that the required level is reached on the first attempt.

texts_at.0: SP performed the directed special requirement with the IP demonstrating the item on the first attempt and calling the entry parameters for SP to set on the second. Settling the entry parameters before a special requirement is begun has not yet been learned. Performance is consistent with a first exposure at this point of the syllabus, where the Training Section still provides assistance. SP is expected to settle the entry parameters and perform the item independently as the technique becomes familiar.
texts_at.1: SP performed the directed special requirement to the level set by the Performance Standards, with the item completed at the lower limit of acceptability after continuous verbal guidance, due to control inputs applied without a settled reference at the start of the item. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to settle the entry parameters before the item begins rather than adjusting them into it.
texts_at.2: SP performed the directed special requirement to the level set by the Performance Standards, with the required level reached only on the second presentation, due to an initial entry flown from an unsettled aircraft state. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to confirm the aircraft state is settled before every presentation, not only after the first one falls short.
texts_at.3: SP performed the directed special requirement to the level required by the Performance Standards for this training unit, accurately and without delay, with entry parameters settled a beat later than ideal on one presentation. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to settle entry parameters with the same timing on every presentation as consistently as the others.

texts_above.1: SP performed the directed special requirement to the level set by the Performance Standards, with the item completed at the lower limit of acceptability before it was stabilized. The stabilization followed continuous verbal guidance from the IP. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the shortfall, reset the parameters and reflew the item to a level between the required and the fully proficient standard, on its own initiative and without IP intervention, after the first presentation had been flown from an unsettled aircraft state. Confirming the aircraft state is settled before every presentation, not only after the first one falls short, would remove the need for that reflight. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to solid entry-parameter discipline.
texts_above.3: SP performed the directed special requirement to the level required by the Performance Standards for this training unit, accurately and without delay, with entry parameters established before the item was begun and held throughout its execution. The only refinement available is to settle entry parameters with the same timing on every presentation as consistently as the others. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to well-developed entry-parameter discipline.
texts_above.4: SP performed the directed special requirement to a standard above the level set for this training unit, with deviations negligible throughout and entry, execution and recovery flown as one continuous sequence with no correcting input of significance. There is little left to refine; the item already requires no repetition and no comment. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to outstanding entry-parameter discipline.

error_modes.label: INTEGRATION OF THE SPECIAL REQUIREMENT INTO THE SORTIE WORKLOAD

texts.0: SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, did not insert the directed special requirement at a point of the profile where it could be flown correctly. SP began the item while still re-programming the navigation aid and running the descent checks, and the instrument scan collapsed at the entry. The IP intervened, stopped the item and re-established the aircraft before it was attempted again.
texts.1: SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not protect the directed special requirement from the surrounding cockpit tasks. SP started the item with the checks unfinished and re-ordered the sequence only after repeated verbal direction from the IP to complete the configuration first. The item was flown to an acceptable level, but the ordering was imposed from the front cockpit.
texts.2: SP, due to an ATC frequency change that arrived at the planned entry point, did not initially separate the directed special requirement from the radio workload. SP recognized the conflict, delayed the entry until the transmission and read-back were complete and then flew the item without further interruption. The re-sequencing was made by SP and no IP intervention was required.
texts.3: SP integrated the directed special requirement into the sortie so that it was flown clear of competing cockpit tasks. Checks, radio work and navigation setup were completed before the entry, and the workload during the item was limited to flying it. The whole sequence was managed without IP intervention and within the planned working time.
texts.4: SP sequenced the directed special requirement so that every competing task was cleared well before the entry, and the item itself was flown with capacity to spare. SP absorbed an unplanned radio call and a block change without any effect on the execution or on the timing of the profile. No task had to be deferred and no IP input was needed.
texts.marginal: SP integrated the directed special requirement into the sortie and the item was flown to standard. However, the entry was begun with the descent checks completed only moments before, and the scan showed a short lag at the start of the item. SP is expected to close out competing cockpit tasks earlier so that the special requirement is entered with the workload already clear.

texts_at.0: SP integrated the directed special requirement into the sortie with the IP completing the configuration first on the first entry and calling the sequence for SP to follow on the second. Completing checks and navigation setup before a competing item is entered has not yet been learned. The maneuver is being introduced at this point of the syllabus, so no independent standard is required yet. SP is expected to complete competing tasks and enter the item independently as the sequence becomes familiar.
texts_at.1: SP integrated the directed special requirement into the sortie with the item begun while checks and navigation setup were still being finished, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to complete checks and navigation setup before the turn, not concurrent with it.
texts_at.2: SP integrated the directed special requirement into the sortie with the sequence re-ordered only after IP direction to complete the configuration first, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to re-order competing tasks on its own initiative before the item is entered, not after direction.
texts_at.3: SP integrated the directed special requirement into the sortie so it was flown clear of competing cockpit tasks, with checks, radio work and navigation setup completed before the entry, due to the scan showing a short lag at the start of one item. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to clear the scan lag with the same margin on every entry as consistently as the others.

texts_above.1: SP integrated the directed special requirement into the sortie with the item begun while checks and navigation setup were still being finished, before the sequence was reordered. The reordering followed a verbal call from the IP directing the configuration to be completed first. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the conflict, delayed the entry until the transmission and read-back were complete and then flew the item without further interruption, with the re-sequencing made without IP intervention, after an ATC frequency change had initially conflicted with the planned entry point. Re-ordering competing tasks on its own initiative before the item is entered, rather than after direction, would remove that conflict at the source. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to steady workload-sequencing discipline.
texts_above.3: SP integrated the directed special requirement into the sortie so it was flown clear of competing cockpit tasks, with checks, radio work and navigation setup completed before the entry and the workload during the item limited to flying it. The only refinement available is to clear the scan lag with the same margin on every entry as consistently as the others. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to consistently accurate workload-sequencing discipline.
texts_above.4: SP sequenced the directed special requirement so every competing task was cleared well before the entry, with the item itself flown with capacity to spare and an unplanned radio call and a block change absorbed without effect on execution or timing. There is little left to refine; no task is ever deferred and no IP input is ever needed. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to exemplary workload-sequencing discipline.

error_modes.label: COMPLIANCE WITH THE RESTRICTIONS ATTACHED TO THE SPECIAL REQUIREMENT
error_modes.source: general:reference_text (Training Exercises analysis + Performance Standards / MIF)

texts.0: SP, due to a working plan built without the limits published for the directed item, did not observe the restrictions attached to the special requirement of this training unit. SP flew the item below the briefed minimum altitude and outside the assigned block, with no recognition of either exceedance. The IP intervened, took control and repositioned the aircraft inside the cleared airspace and above the floor.
texts.1: SP, due to a floor and block that were never cross-checked against the altimeter during the item, did not keep the directed special requirement inside its published restrictions. SP reached the briefed minimum altitude and returned above it only after two direct calls from the IP. The restriction was ultimately respected, but the margin was consumed and the correction came from the front cockpit.
texts.2: SP, due to a descent rate that was allowed to build at the entry, did not initially protect the altitude margin required for the directed special requirement. SP recognized the trend against the altimeter while still well above the briefed floor, arrested the descent and completed the item inside the assigned block. The restriction was maintained throughout and no IP intervention was required.
texts.3: SP complied with all the restrictions attached to the directed special requirement, keeping the item inside the assigned block, above the briefed floor and within the aircraft limits. SP checked the applicable limit before the entry and monitored it against the instruments during the execution. The item was completed without any exceedance and without IP intervention.
texts.4: SP complied with every restriction attached to the directed special requirement with a comfortable margin maintained throughout, and stated the applicable limits aloud before the entry. The item was contained within the block and above the floor at all times, with no approach to any boundary. No correction and no IP comment were required.
texts.marginal: SP complied with the restrictions attached to the directed special requirement and no limit was exceeded. However, the item was flown close to the lower edge of the assigned block on both presentations, leaving little margin if the recovery had required more altitude. SP is expected to plan the entry higher within the block so that the published floor is protected by a working margin rather than by a late correction.

texts_at.0: SP complied with the restrictions attached to the special requirement with the IP building the working plan from the published limits on the first item and calling the altimeter check for SP to make on the second. Building the working plan directly from the published limits, rather than from habit, has not yet been learned. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to build the working plan from the published limits independently as the habit becomes established.
texts_at.1: SP complied with the restrictions attached to the directed special requirement, with the briefed minimum altitude reached and returned above it only after two direct calls, due to a working plan built without the limits published for the directed item. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to build the working plan directly from the published limits, not from habit.
texts_at.2: SP complied with the restrictions attached to the directed special requirement, with the altitude margin initially not protected before a descent rate allowed to build was arrested, due to a descent rate that was allowed to build at the entry. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to set the entry rate of descent with the margin already planned in, not corrected into it.
texts_at.3: SP complied with all the restrictions attached to the directed special requirement, keeping the item inside the assigned block, above the briefed floor and within the aircraft limits, with the applicable limit checked a beat later than ideal before one entry. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to check the applicable limit before every entry with the same timing as the others.

texts_above.1: SP complied with the restrictions attached to the directed special requirement, with the briefed minimum altitude reached and returned above it only after two direct calls. The calls came as verbal directions from the IP naming the altitude. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the trend against the altimeter while still well above the briefed floor, arrested the descent and completed the item inside the assigned block, without IP intervention, after the descent rate had initially been allowed to build at the entry. Setting the entry rate of descent with the margin already planned in, rather than corrected into it, would remove the need for that recognition. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to dependable restriction-compliance discipline.
texts_above.3: SP complied with all the restrictions attached to the directed special requirement, keeping the item inside the assigned block, above the briefed floor and within the aircraft limits, checking the applicable limit before the entry and monitoring it against the instruments during execution. The only refinement available is to check the applicable limit before every entry with the same timing as the others. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to notably good restriction-compliance discipline.
texts_above.4: SP complied with every restriction attached to the directed special requirement with a comfortable margin maintained throughout, stating the applicable limits aloud before the entry and containing the item within the block and above the floor at all times. There is little left to refine; no correction and no IP comment are ever required. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to superior restriction-compliance discipline.

error_modes.label: COORDINATION WITH THE IP AND RESPONSE TO DIRECTION ON THE SPECIAL REQUIREMENT

texts.0: SP, due to failure to pass a required call at the briefed point, did not coordinate the execution of the directed special requirement with the IP. SP began and abandoned the item twice without announcing either the entry or the reason for the discontinuation, so the rear cockpit had no picture of the intended sequence. The IP intervened, took control and re-established a common plan before the item was flown again.
texts.1: SP, due to an indirect hint instead of a direct statement of the aircraft state, did not make clear that the directed special requirement was being deferred. SP restated the intention only after the IP had asked twice what was being flown and why the briefed sequence had changed. The coordination was restored, but only through direct questioning from the front cockpit.
texts.2: SP, due to an entry call made after the item had already begun, did not initially keep the IP informed of the sequence being flown. SP recognized the gap, announced the remaining plan for the special requirement and confirmed each subsequent entry and completion before acting. The remainder of the item was flown with the IP fully in the picture and without intervention.
texts.3: SP coordinated the directed special requirement with the IP throughout, announcing the entry, the parameters being set and the completion of each item. Direction received from the front cockpit was read back and applied without delay. The whole sequence was flown with a shared picture of the plan and required no intervention.
texts.4: SP kept the IP fully informed at every stage of the directed special requirement, stating the intention, the entry conditions and the outcome of each item without being asked. When the IP offered a refinement of technique, SP applied it on the next presentation with an immediate and visible improvement. The coordination was complete, standard and entirely SP-initiated.
texts.marginal: SP coordinated the directed special requirement with the IP and the shared picture was maintained, so the standard was met. However, two entry calls were made simultaneously with the control input rather than before it, and one item was completed without any call at all. SP is expected to announce the intention before acting so that the IP is briefed on the sequence rather than informed of it after the fact.

texts_at.0: SP coordinated the special requirement with the IP asking directly what was being flown on the first item and prompting the intention for SP to state on the second. Stating the aircraft state and intention directly, rather than with an indirect hint, has not yet been learned. Performance is consistent with a first exposure at this point of the syllabus, where the Training Section still provides assistance. SP is expected to state the intention directly and coordinate independently as the habit becomes established.
texts_at.1: SP coordinated the execution of the directed special requirement with the IP, with the intention restated only after the IP asked twice what was being flown, due to an indirect hint instead of a direct statement of the aircraft state. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to state the aircraft state and intention directly the first time, not after being asked a second time.
texts_at.2: SP coordinated the execution of the directed special requirement with the IP, with the sequence announced only after the item had already begun, due to an entry call made after the item had already begun. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to make the entry call before beginning the item, not after.
texts_at.3: SP coordinated the directed special requirement with the IP throughout, announcing the entry, the parameters being set and the completion of each item, with one call made a beat later than ideal on one occasion. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to make every coordination call with the same timing as the others.

texts_above.1: SP coordinated the execution of the directed special requirement, with the intention restated only after being asked twice what was being flown. The questions came as verbal calls from the IP. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the gap, announced the remaining plan for the special requirement and confirmed each subsequent entry and completion before acting, without IP intervention, after an entry call had initially been made after the item had already begun. Making the entry call before beginning the item, rather than after, would remove that gap entirely. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to assured coordination discipline.
texts_above.3: SP coordinated the directed special requirement with the IP throughout, announcing the entry, the parameters being set and the completion of each item, with direction received from the front cockpit read back and applied without delay. The only refinement available is to make every coordination call with the same timing as the others. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to precise coordination discipline.
texts_above.4: SP kept the IP fully informed at every stage of the directed special requirement, stating the intention, the entry conditions and the outcome of each item without being asked, and applied an offered refinement of technique on the next presentation with an immediate and visible improvement. There is little left to refine; the coordination is already entirely self-initiated. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to first-rate coordination discipline.
